title: Keep SIPs going through falls
objectives: Explain why SIPs are designed for falls, and what to do when cash is tight.
Say what stopping a SIP gives up.
body_md:
SIPs are designed for falls: the same amount buys more units when prices are low. Stopping a SIP in a fall gives up the cheapest units. If cash is genuinely tight, pause for a short period rather than redeeming, and restart.

> **Investor takeaway:** You can't control the date you started. You can control whether you stay, keep investing and stick to the plan.
example: Market fell 15%, SIP running: the same ₹10,000 buys more units this month — stopping skips the cheapest units.
say: Stopping a SIP in a fall gives up the cheapest units.
If cash is tight, pause briefly rather than redeem.
never: Stopping a SIP protects you in a fall.

check.q: “It was obvious the market would crash” reflects…
check.why: Hindsight bias. Events look predictable only after they happen.

check.q: A client’s cash is genuinely tight during a fall. What’s the better option for the SIP?
o: Pause the SIP briefly rather than redeem
check.why: Pause the SIP briefly rather than redeem. Pausing keeps existing units invested; redeeming locks in the fall.

check.q: A client's cash is genuinely tight during a fall. What is the better SIP option?
o: Pause the SIP briefly rather than redeem
check.why: If cash is genuinely tight, pause for a short period rather than redeeming, and restart.
